name: Abanyom
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Asinya, O.E. 1987. A reconstruction of the segmental phonology of Bakor (an Ekoid Bantu language). MA thesis, University of Port Harcourt.
earlier_scan.note: Unpublished offline thesis; segmental focus, stress coverage uncertain; Abanyom described as tonal (Wikipedia, uncited).

sources.citation: Watters, John R. 2001. Some phonological characteristics of Ejagham (Etung), an Ekoid Bantu language of Cameroon and Nigeria. In N. M. Mutaka & S. B. Chumbow (eds.), Research mate in African linguistics: focus on Cameroon, 55-78. Köln: Rüdiger Köppe.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 6 Stress, p. 67: 'In Ejagham, stress falls primarily on the first syllable of the root of the word. Predictable pitch is not one of its phonetic features since any of six tones can occur on this syllable. Neither is any increased loudness noticeable.. So stress does not appear to be phonologically significant in the synchronic system.' This describes Ejagham (ejag1239), a sister Ekoid language, not Abanyom.
States only 'The language is tonal' (uncited) and cites Asinya 1987; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2020. An atlas of Nigerian languages (4th ed. draft). Cambridge: KWEF. Entry 35 'Bakor cluster', 35.a Abanyom.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on phonology; lists refs for the cluster: Wordlist Koelle (1854: 11), Thomas (1914: 8), Winston (1964: 77), Crabb (1965: 7); Comparative Asinya (1987); Survey Yoder et al. (2008); for Nkum 'Phonology: Asinya (1985)'.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. [2011 circulation draft; Glottolog ref 319477 dates it 2014]. Ekoid: Bantoid languages of the Nigeria-Cameroun borderland. Ms., 27 pp. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 3 Phonology (pp. 5-6) treats consonants, vowels and tone for Ekoid as a group ('Both Mbe and Ekoid have High, Low, Rising, Falling and Downstep tones..'); no mention of stress or accent anywhere in the 27 pp. Abanyom appears only as language Q in the comparative wordlist.

sources.citation: Yoder, Zachariah, Katarína Hannelová & Linus Otronyi. 2008 (24 Sept.). A summary of the sociolinguistic survey of the Bakor languages of Cross River State, Nigeria. 12 pp. + Appendix 2 Bakor wordlists (30 pp.). Composite PDF hosted by R. Blench.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sociolinguistic survey (intelligibility, vitality, literacy) plus tone-marked 361-item wordlists in 11 Bakor varieties incl. Q-Abanyom (Abonima-Nkim village, 2008); no phonological statement, no stress. Sec. 1.3 says the only linguistic work since Crabb 1965 was an initial survey by Russ Anderson (1977-).
